trend.name: Trend following
trend.summary: Buys assets in established uptrends (price above rising 1h/4h EMAs) that break out of their recent range.
trend.rationale: Crypto returns show time-series momentum: flows, leverage and narrative feedback make trends persist longer than a random walk implies. Trend entries with ATR stops keep losers small and let winners run.
trend.evaluation: Backtested against buy-and-hold BTC and a no-AI version of the same screen. Paper: win rate, payoff ratio and expectancy per trade after fees, by market regime.
trend.ai_role: Checks whether the trend has a fundamental driver or shows signs of exhaustion (crowding, a fading catalyst, upcoming supply unlocks).

daily_trend.name: Long-term trend
daily_trend.summary: Holds assets in a long-term uptrend (50-day average above the 200-day, price above the 200-day) for weeks to months, bought above the 50-day or on a pullback to it.
daily_trend.rationale: The same time-series momentum as the trend screen, on the timeframe where it is strongest and cheapest to harvest: few trades, so fees barely matter, and daily-ATR stops ride out the intraday noise that stops short-term trades.
daily_trend.evaluation: Compared with buy-and-hold of the same assets: does stepping aside below the long-term trend cut drawdowns more than it costs in missed upside? Paper: return per trade after costs and holding time.
daily_trend.ai_role: Checks that the long-term story still holds (adoption, flows, supply) and that a pullback is a dip, not the start of a breakdown.

mean_reversion.name: Mean reversion
mean_reversion.summary: Buys sharp, oversold dislocations (RSI < 30 below the lower Bollinger band) in assets whose daily trend is intact.
mean_reversion.rationale: Liquidation cascades and forced selling overshoot fair value on short horizons. If nothing fundamental changed, prices tend to snap back part of the move.
mean_reversion.evaluation: Measured on forward 6-48h returns vs the no-AI screen. The key question is whether AI filtering of 'real news' selloffs improves the hit rate enough to beat costs.
mean_reversion.ai_role: Decides whether the drop is noise (liquidations, a temporary flow) or information (a hack, delisting, regulatory action). The latter is a no-trade.

momentum.name: Relative strength
momentum.summary: Ranks the universe by volatility-adjusted 7d/30d returns and proposes the leaders when the broad market regime is not risk-off.
momentum.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum: capital rotates into leading assets, and leaders keep outperforming laggards over days to weeks.
momentum.evaluation: Compared with an equal-weight basket of the universe and with BTC. Tracks turnover, because rotation costs fees.
momentum.ai_role: Looks for the reason behind the strength and flags correlation: five leaders that are all the same trade count as one bet.

event_driven.name: Event driven
event_driven.summary: Reacts to abnormal price/volume shocks and catalysts found in research: listings, upgrades, ETF flows, macro releases.
event_driven.rationale: Markets take time to digest complex news. A verified catalyst that is not yet priced in can offer a short-lived edge; unverified rumors cannot.
event_driven.evaluation: Every event decision records the catalyst and whether it was verified; outcomes are scored by forward returns after costs.
event_driven.ai_role: Primary driver: researches and verifies the catalyst, judges how much is priced in, and refuses to trade unverified claims.

discretionary.name: On-demand evaluation
discretionary.summary: Pairs the owner asks the AI to evaluate right now, outside the screens. Same research, decision and risk checks as any candidate.
discretionary.rationale: Not a strategy with an edge of its own: a way to put a specific pair in front of the research desk (a catalyst you noticed, or simply to test the pipeline). Tracked separately so it can't flatter the screened strategies.
discretionary.evaluation: Scored like every decision (forward returns after costs). Disable it if it doesn't earn its keep.
discretionary.ai_role: Everything: with no screen signal behind it, the AI has to find a reason to trade, and no_trade is the expected default.

core.name: Trend core
core.summary: Rules, not the AI: while BTC is above its 50-day average, holds the strongest coins in a long-term uptrend (above a 50-day average that is above the 200-day, ranked by 30-day return per unit of daily volatility), each risking 1% of equity at a 2.5-ATR stop that trails winners.
core.rationale: Time-series momentum is crypto's best-documented edge, and it pays through a few large trends: being invested in them, with losses cut at the stop and winners left to run, matters more than picking entries. Rules don't hesitate, trim winners or sit in cash.
core.evaluation: Compared with holding BTC and an equal-weight basket of the universe over the same weeks: return, drawdown, and how much of each trend it caught after fees.
core.ai_role: An overlay: news negative enough to veto an entry blocks it, and the agent may close a core position only when news about it woke the agent.

long_term.name: Long-term book
long_term.summary: Rules, not the AI: holds BTC (25% of equity) and ETH (15%) for the long term, through short-term swings, and sells one only after a week closing below its 200-day average (buying it back after a week closing above).
long_term.rationale: Most of crypto's return has come from a few long bull markets. Holding the two largest coins through them, and stepping aside only when the long-term trend breaks, captures that without trading the noise.
long_term.evaluation: Compared with simply holding BTC and ETH: does stepping aside below the 200-day average cut drawdowns more than it costs in missed upside?
long_term.ai_role: None in its rules; the agent may close one of its positions only when news about it woke the agent.
